answer: Each established agent may issue at most two invitations a year. To activate one, the invitee locks 1,000 tokens and the inviter posts a matching 1,000 as surety. A clerk writes a crystal record of both locks in the public karst ledger and treats that pair as the identity's anchor. One hundred fakes therefore need 50 inviters and 200,000 tokens at risk. Buying leftover invitations fails because each inviter's surety stays bound to every invitee they sponsor. An honest agent pays the 1,000 once, and both locks return after twelve clean epochs.
